_comment: Interview questions per area. 'probe' is the concrete follow-up that turns a self-claim into a supported one: it asks for something only someone who has actually done the thing can answer. Edit freely; the bot reads this file.

questions.ask: How would you describe your Python?
questions.probe: What is the last thing you built with it, and what did it do?
What did you use it for most recently?

questions.ask: How comfortable are you with algorithms and data structures?
questions.probe: Which problems or judges have you practised on, roughly how many?

questions.ask: Have you written any Verilog or VHDL?
questions.probe: Which board or tool did you use, and what did you make run on it?

questions.ask: How about circuits and electronics generally?
questions.probe: What have you actually built or measured?

questions.ask: How much mathematical modelling have you done?
questions.probe: Which model or paper did you work on, and what was your part in it?

questions.ask: How is your written English for a report or paper?
questions.probe: What is the longest thing you have written in English, and for what?

questions.ask: Realistically, how many hours a week can you give a contest?
Do you already have a team you would enter with?
What are you hoping to get out of this (postgraduate recommendation, experience, a specific contest)?
